forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Pyramid Park and Q-Park Disposal - Cabinet Report - Part A (1)
findings.headline: Disposal will reduce revenue costs of holding long-term vacant sites, but ongoing annual cost is not quantified
findings.detail: The council has been bearing revenue costs to maintain, hold and secure Pyramid Park (7.4 acres vacant for over 15 years) and Q-Park (1 acre vacant since 2009). The paper states that disposal will reduce these revenue costs, but does not quantify the current annual costs or the expected savings from disposal, making it impossible to assess the materiality of this revenue benefit.
findings.matters: Ongoing costs to hold derelict sites represent a drag on the council's revenue budget; the actual size of this saving is not disclosed.
findings.figures: Pyramid Park: 7.4 acres, vacant over 15 years; Q-Park: 1 acre, vacant since 2009; annual holding costs not specified
findings.quote: reduce the revenue costs of holding, maintaining and securing these long-term vacant, town centre opportunity sites

findings.paper_title: Pyramid Park and Q-Park Disposal - Cabinet Report - Part A (1)
findings.headline: Q-Park has multiple existing leasehold interests with incomplete title clarity, risking disposal delays
findings.detail: Q-Park site is subject to six leases including three occupational leases held by Q-Park Ltd (car park operator), NHS Property Services Limited, and Six Town Housing Limited. The council has not completed title due diligence, noting that a title review will be undertaken as soon as possible to identify all third-party rights. These leasehold interests may affect the timing of the proposed development, with potential to delay financial completion and threaten the 31 March 2027 grant deadline.
findings.matters: Incomplete title certainty and multiple occupational leases create legal and timing risks that could delay the development, push past the BLRF2 deadline, and jeopardise the £1.73m grant.
findings.figures: Six leases affecting Q-Park site, three occupational leases identified
findings.quote: It is understood that there are six leases affecting the site, including three apparent occupational leases. Given the wider leasehold structure, a title review will be undertaken as soon as possible

findings.paper_title: Pyramid Park and Q-Park Disposal - Cabinet Report - Part A (1)
findings.headline: Section 106 planning obligations will reduce the net capital receipt from disposal, but amount is not disclosed
findings.detail: The paper acknowledges that planning obligations will impact the land value received but does not quantify these obligations. Section 106 contributions can be substantial, meaning the actual capital receipt to the council will be lower than the red book valuation. The decision on final disposal terms and capital receipt has been delegated to executives specifically because of this uncertainty.
findings.matters: Unquantified Section 106 obligations represent downside to the financial case made for this disposal and create uncertainty about the actual benefit to the council's finances.
findings.figures: Amount of Section 106 contributions not specified in Part A
findings.quote: the eventual land offer is likely to be impacted by Section 106 contributions obligated through the planning approval process

findings.paper_title: Pyramid Park and Q-Park Disposal - Cabinet Report - Part A (1)
findings.headline: £1.73m BLRF2 grant faces full clawback if disposal milestone of 31 March 2027 is missed
findings.detail: The council received £1.73m in BLRF2 grant funding conditional on disposing Pyramid Park to a developer by 31 March 2027 and having new homes completed by 31 March 2029. The paper explicitly warns that failure to meet these milestones creates a risk of grant clawback. Remediation works are underway with autumn 2026 completion expected, leaving a tight timeline to secure developer completion and financial closure by March 2027.
findings.matters: A £1.73m clawback would be material to the council's financial position and would also jeopardise the anticipated capital receipt, creating a double-hit to their balance sheet and budget.
findings.figures: £1.73 million grant funding, disposal deadline 31 March 2027, homes completion deadline 31 March 2029, remediation completion autumn 2026
findings.quote: This risks a full grant claw back of the £1.73 million brownfield funding provided by One Public Estate (OPE)

findings.headline: Treasury investment balances fell 29% to £14.6m, reducing financial flexibility and internal borrowing capacity
findings.detail: Council's treasury investments declined from £20.7m to £14.6m (£6.1m reduction), representing all surplus cash and reserves. Cash now represents only 4% of gross borrowing compared to 7% previously, indicating council is increasingly externally financed and has limited capacity to internally self-manage cash flows.
findings.matters: Significantly reduces council's buffer to absorb timing differences between income and expenditure; increases dependence on external debt markets; limits ability to avoid external borrowing through internal resource management
findings.figures: Treasury investments £20.7m to £14.618m (reduction £6.082m, -29%); cash as % of gross borrowing declined from 7.0% to 4.0%
findings.quote: As of 31 March 2026, the council held £14.618m of invested funds, representing income received in advance of expenditure plus balances and reserves held
